feedback: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry yet, so this review rests only on the contract and the candidate's own contents. The candidate is valid: every value is inside its contract limit, and the sensor weights are antisymmetric (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal has the right sign and scale. Two points to watch once it races. (1) kp = 4 with weights up to |2| gives turn up to 8, or about 2800 PWM of differential. At a full-scale edge reading, the inner wheel command can clamp near zero, so sharp bends may be taken with one wheel nearly stopped. (2) base_speed = 1.6 gives a base PWM of about 2620. That is needed to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s the 3 s limit requires, but it leaves little headroom on the tightest bends. Plan the next revision from the race, as follows. If the run goes off track or shows line_loss_events on the sharpest bend, lower base_speed to about 1.2 to 1.4 before changing gains. If it completes with high steering_oscillation on the slalom, raise kd to about 0.6 to 0.8 before changing kp. If it completes with rms_error well above what the bends require and completion_time near 3 s, the gains are sound and base_speed is the lever to push up. Because this is the first race, approving it now gives the telemetry that will sharpen every later critique.
requested_changes: If the robot leaves the track or loses the line on the tightest bend, reduce base_speed to about 1.2 to 1.4 before touching the gains. Basis: base_speed 1.6 was chosen from first principles, not measured, and the contract's sharp-bend risk is the main unknown.
If steering_oscillation is high on the slalom, raise kd to about 0.6 to 0.8 and hold kp at 4. Basis: kd = 0.4 was chosen to damp sensor lag, and no race has yet shown whether that is enough.

If the run completes but completion_time is close to 3 s with low rms_error, keep the gains and raise base_speed in small steps (about 0.1 to 0.2) while watching max_error. Basis: the 1.5 m/s average the limit requires is not yet confirmed as reachable.
